judge_assessment.explanation: The mathematics survives independent checking and the ACCEPT is defensible, but two judge statements do not survive the artifacts. (1) The judge lists the verified results as '... three rectangles, 3<4, and equal four-corner counts'. Problem 6's comparison is 2 < 4, not 3 < 4: the Group A tikz in worksheet.tex draws a square balanced on a corner, a rotated rectangle and a triangle, so two four-sided shapes; verify.json id 6 is {'values': [2, 4], 'expected': '<'} and the answer key prints '2 < 4' with the reasoning 'Group A holds ... so two four-sided shapes'. The relation is right, the count the judge cites is not. (2) The judge scored answer_key_quality 4 without opening the Quick Answers bank. answer_key.pdf prints '2. -', '6. -' and '7. -' -- three fully verified relations ('>', '<', '=') rendered as the exact glyph that row '8. -' uses for the one genuinely manual item. A grader looking at that bank cannot tell which of those four rows was checked and which was left to a human. The mechanism is the known render_quick_answers._fmt bug: sympify('<') raises and the handler falls back to '---'. Everything else the judge asserts checks out -- 3 triangles (A, D, F), 2 squares (B, E), 1 circle (C), 4 tilted triangles in problem 3, 3 rectangles in problem 5, and 4 = 4 corners in problem 7.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 4 draws a square balanced on a corner and makes the child count before naming it, and the key answers the 'diamond' objection precisely rather than by contradiction: "'Diamond' tells you which way it is turned; 'square' tells you what it is", followed by 'you can call it a diamond if you like -- and it is still a square.'
Problem 7 draws the SAME square twice, flat and turned, and asks for a corner count on each so the invariance the sheet teaches becomes a countable 4 = 4 rather than an assertion.

Problem 8's manual entry gives two objective checks -- three straight sides that close, and a reason that names something countable -- plus the instruction not to mark a flat triangle wrong but to ask the child to turn the paper.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt routes every string expected through bare sympy.sympify. A relation string raises SympifyError/SyntaxError and the handler returns '---', which render_entry also returns for manual-only problems, so 'verified' and 'nobody checked this' print identically in the delivered answer key.
evidence: scripts/render_quick_answers.py lines 57-61: string branch is try: sympy.latex(sympy.sympify(v)) except ...: return '---'.
verify.json ids 2, 6, 7 are type 'compare' with order 'relation' and expecteds '>', '<', '=' -- all machine-verified; id 8 is the only 'manual'.

root_causes.description: Coverage is enforced per problem id, not per printed response slot, so a problem that prints several blanks satisfies the gate with one entry. Here the single most important answer on the sheet -- the NAME of the shape in problem 4 -- is an unverified blank.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 4 prints three response slots: '...How many sides?~\ansblank', '...How many corners?~\ansblank', and 'so its name is \underline{\hspace{3cm}}'. verify.json id 4 has two entries, sides=4 and corners=4; nothing checks that the name is 'square'.

Problems 2, 6 and 7 each print both numeral blanks plus the relation blank (e.g. 'Group A has~\ansblank ... Group B has~\ansblank ... Write $>$, $<$, or $=$'), and each carries exactly one compare entry whose counts live in 'values' as inputs rather than as verified expecteds.

Problem 7 additionally ends 'and tell your grown-up what that tells you about the name of the turned shape' with no manual entry, while the parallel explanation in problem 8 is correctly flagged manual.

improvements.title: Typeset verified comparison relations in the Quick Answers bank instead of a manual-review dash
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, special-case relation strings ('<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=', '!=') before the sympify call and render them together with the entry's compared 'values', e.g. '$2 < 4$', so the row shows a checkable answer. Separately, stop using the same glyph for two meanings: render_entry should emit a distinct marker for manual-only rows (for example 'see key') so a grader reading '2. -' next to '8. -' can tell which was machine-verified.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_render_quick_answers.py assert that render_entry([{'id': 6, 'type': 'compare', 'values': [2, 4], 'order': 'relation', 'expected': '<'}]) returns text containing the relation and NOT equal to '---', and that a manual-only entry returns a marker distinct from any verified row. Both assertions fail against today's _fmt and pass after the change.
improvements.expected_impact: Three of eight rows in this key stop being blank, and across the suite every verified comparison becomes gradeable from the bank, restoring the distinction between 'verified' and 'manual'.
improvements.risk: The bank widens, which feeds render_quick_answers.column_count and can drop a key from four columns to three; page budget for the answer key should be re-checked on the longest cases.

improvements.title: Require a verify entry for every printed answer slot, including the shape-name blank in problem 4
improvements.proposed_change: Change the SKILL.md coverage rule from 'every problem id has at least one check' to 'every rendered answer-location macro has a check or an explicit manual entry', and extend tests/check_layout.py to count \ansblank, \ansline and bare \underline{\hspace{...}} response rules inside each \problem body against the expecteds bound to that id. For this case that forces a read_data or compare entry for problem 4's name blank ('square') and entries for the numeral blanks in problems 2, 6 and 7 rather than leaving those counts as bare inputs in 'values'.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet with a problem printing three response rules (two \ansblank plus one \underline{\hspace{3cm}}) and only two verify entries: tests/check_layout.py must exit non-zero naming the uncovered rule. Today this shape builds green (curr-046 problem 4 did); after the fix it fails and the three-entry variant passes.
improvements.expected_impact: The answer a shapes sheet exists to elicit -- the shape's name -- stops being the one thing on the page nobody checked, and comparison problems verify their operands as well as the relation.
improvements.risk: Existing verify.json files across the corpus will start failing until back-filled; the macro counter must not treat header rules or figure labels as response slots.

improvements.title: Flag problem 7's spoken explanation as manual instead of recording it only as a compare
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate that scans each problem's worksheet prose for explanation cues ('tell your grown-up', 'explain', 'say why', 'how you know', 'tell a friend') and fails unless that problem id carries a manual entry. SKILL.md already directs authors to use manual for any explanation or reasoning answer, but nothing enforces it, which is why problem 7's 'tell your grown-up what that tells you about the name of the turned shape' is recorded solely as compare while the identical demand in problem 8 is flagged.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with a problem whose text contains 'tell your grown-up what that tells you' and only a compare entry: the gate exits non-zero; the same fixture with an added manual entry for that id passes. Fails today, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Manual-review counts reported to the adult become accurate, and open items get the grading guidance the manual desc field carries.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will produce false positives on prose that merely narrates ('the key explains ...'); the rule should look only inside \problem bodies and should be overridable with an explicit author annotation.

case_summary: A strong orientation-invariance sheet: every shape is drawn turned, every classification in the key matches its tikz, and the counts I recomputed from the source (3/2/1 in Shape Set One, 4 tilted triangles, 3 rectangles, 2 vs 4 four-sided shapes, 4 = 4 corners) all agree with verify.json. Problem 8 is correctly flagged manual with objective criteria. Two defects the judge did not reach: the delivered Quick Answers bank prints a manual-style dash for three verified relations, and coverage is slot-blind -- problem 4's shape-name blank, the very answer the lesson is about, has no verify entry, and problem 7's spoken explanation is unflagged. The judge's '3<4' for problem 6 is a misreport of a comparison that is actually 2 < 4.
